grammar_textbook_based.topic: Present perfect simple (with just, already and yet)

structures.title: Present perfect simple (with just, already and yet)
structures.content: This structure is used to talk about actions that happened at an unspecified time before now. The time is not important. You can use 'just', 'already', and 'yet' with the present perfect tense.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Present perfect simple (with for and since)

structures.title: Present perfect simple (with for and since)
structures.content: This structure is used to talk about actions that started in the past and continue to the present. 'For' is used for periods of time, and 'since' is used for points in time.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Present perfect simple vs. past simple

structures.title: Present perfect simple vs. past simple
structures.content: The present perfect tense is used for actions that have a connection to the present. The past simple tense is used for actions that happened at a specific time in the past.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Articles (a, an, the or no article)

structures.title: Articles (a, an, the or no article)
structures.content: Articles are used before nouns. 'A' and 'an' are indefinite articles, 'the' is a definite article, and sometimes no article is used.

structures.title: Adverbs of manner and comparison
structures.content: Adverbs of manner describe how something is done. Adverbs of comparison are used to compare two things.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Indefinite pronouns (everyone, no one, someone, etc.)

structures.title: Indefinite pronouns (everyone, no one, someone, etc.)
structures.content: Indefinite pronouns refer to people or things without specifying which ones.

structures.title: Present perfect continuous
structures.content: This structure is used to talk about actions that started in the past and continue to the present, often with a result in the present.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Present perfect continuous vs. present perfect simple

structures.title: Present perfect continuous vs. present perfect simple
structures.content: The present perfect continuous emphasizes the duration of an action, while the present perfect simple emphasizes the completion of an action.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Future forms (using: present simple, present continuous, going to, will/won't)

structures.title: Future forms (using: present simple, present continuous, going to, will/won't)
structures.content: These structures are used to talk about future events. The present simple is used for scheduled events, the present continuous for planned events, 'going to' for intentions, and 'will/won't' for predictions and instant decisions.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: The passive (present simple, past simple, present continuous, present perfect)

structures.title: The passive (present simple, past simple, present continuous, present perfect)
structures.content: The passive voice is used when the focus is on the action rather than the doer of the action. It is formed using a form of 'to be' and the past participle.

structures.title: Word formation (from 'root' word)
structures.content: This involves creating new words from a root word by adding prefixes and suffixes.

structures.title: Comparative and superlative adjectives
structures.content: Comparative adjectives compare two things, and superlative adjectives compare three or more things.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Modal verbs to talk about rules and obligation in past and present: must, mustn't, have to, don't have to, had to, didn't have to

structures.title: Modal verbs to talk about rules and obligation in past and present: must, mustn't, have to, don't have to, had to, didn't have to
structures.content: These modal verbs are used to express obligation, necessity, and lack of necessity in the past and present.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Question tags to show interest / request clarification

structures.title: Question tags to show interest / request clarification
structures.content: Question tags are short questions added to the end of a statement to confirm information or show interest.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Present simple and present continuous (always with present continuous)

structures.title: Present simple and present continuous (always with present continuous)
structures.content: The present simple is used for habits and general truths, while the present continuous is used for actions happening now or around now.

structures.title: Past simple vs. past continuous
structures.content: The past simple is used for completed actions, and the past continuous is used for actions in progress at a specific time in the past.

structures.title: The passive (present and past simple)
structures.content: The passive voice is used when the focus is on the action rather than the doer of the action. It is formed using a form of 'to be' and the past participle.

grammar_textbook_based.topic: Infinitive of purpose: She went to the shops to buy a new bag for school.

structures.title: Infinitive of purpose: She went to the shops to buy a new bag for school.
structures.content: The infinitive of purpose is used to express the reason for an action.
